messages:
lee: Heads-up — saw a tenant spike route 95% of traffic to the tiny-quant backup model during the 11:07 surge. Latency exploded and the CB tripped twice.

dana: Ugh, saw that in the dashboard. Canary rollout should have kept primary pinned. Do we have header-based routing leaks? :thinking:

alice: Logs show requests had X-RW-Prefer: low-cost which matched a fallback lane. Route match order currently does prefix -> header -> exact. That means header wins even if capacity is constrained.

ben: Can you paste the snippet? I want to see the lane weights and cb settings.

lee: Sure — from edge-proxy traces: 
```yaml
routes:
  - match: "/v1/generate*"
    priority: 20
    headers:
      X-RW-Prefer: low-cost
    fallback_chain: [quant-small, quant-tiny]
    circuit_breaker:
      max_inflight: 120
      error_threshold_pct: 20
      open_for: 30s
```

alice: Two problems: 1) header-based lane should be soft-match when system CPU/GPU utilization > 80%. 2) fallback_chain order should consider capacity signals, not static list.

sre-jen: Agree. We need a probe that evaluates pool capacity before honoring fallthrough. Something like a quick capacity ping with a TTL to avoid calling probes on every request.

ben: Proposed heuristic: if pool_util > 75% mark header matches as advisory; if CB open then fallback to next healthy model. Also add a short-lived token in header `X-RW-Probe: <id>` so probes are rate-limited.

dana: I can add a telemetry metric: fallback_decision_reason with tags {route, tenant, reason=(cb | cap | header)} so UX can show why the request chose backup. We should expose it in the rollout UI.

lee: UX ask: rollout editor should display the computed fallback_chain and a preview of decisions given simulated load. Right now it only shows static list. Showing simulated path would avoid surprises.

alice: Implementation notes: 
- Add route-level `match_mode` enum: STRICT | ADVISORY. Default existing behavior maps to STRICT.
- Introduce `capacity_probe` config: `{interval: 5s, ttl: 30s, threshold: 0.75}`.
- Change fallback evaluation order to: exact route match -> capacity check -> advisory header -> fallback list.

ben: Also adjust CB tuning: lower `max_inflight` for tiny models on shared pools, raise `error_threshold_pct` for model warmups so short-lived spikes don't trip it.

infra-bot: Deploy plan: create feature flag `route_advisory_headers_v1` scoped to staging and 5 tenants, monitor `fallback_decision_reason`, `model_latency_p95`, `cb_open_count`. Auto-rollback on sustained spike > 5m.

sre-jen: Add dashboards: per-route fallback rates, probe success rate, and per-tenant CB opens. Alert if fallback rate > 10% for > 3m.

dana: I'll wire the telemetry and add a new column in Rollouts -> Routes tab that shows "Fallback expected under load" with a tiny sim button.

lee: Next steps: dana and alice to spec the telemetry + API change, ben to prototype probe middleware, I'll add the feature flag and rollout plan.

alice: Quick question — do we allow tenants to opt-out of advisory headers? Some customers rely on cost headers intentionally.

ben: Yes, make it a tenant opt-in flag; default platform-level is advisory. Document in console and API.

lee: Cool. If no objections I'll open RFC and assign owners. :thumbsup:
